THE HEADLINES:

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates ‘Bharat Parv 2026’ at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat marking the beginning of 151st birth anniversary celebrations of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

  2. Extreme poverty in the country declined from 27.1 per cent in 2011 to 2.6 per cent in 2023, says World Bank’s Poverty and Equity Brief.

  3. In West Bengal, over 7 thousand people evacuated to safer locations as water level of Sankosh River in Alipurduar district rises due to glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan.

  4. Six people died in a helicopter crash at Hathi Parvat hills of Chamoli district in Uttarakhand.

  5. Government announces nationwide Census from 25th January to 28th February, next year, excluding snow and poll-bound states.

  6. And, Manisha Bhanwala becomes first Indian woman to win a gold medal at Wrestling World Championships in Kazakhstan.

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated ‘Bharat Parv 2026’ at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat’s Narmada district today, ahead of the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations. Tomorrow, on the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Prime Minister will pay floral tributes at the Statue of Unity and dedicate multiple development projects to the nation. More from our correspondent –

 

 

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated ‘Bharat Parv’, cultural festival reflecting the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ that will continue till November 15. The Prime Minister is also scheduled to witness the ‘Ekta Prakash Parv’, an illumination festival featuring 530-metre illuminated stretch and a 180-metre Glow Tunnel Tomorrow. Marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Mr. Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for 31 tourism and infrastructure projects over 426 crore rupees. These include IRCTC hotel, the Ekta Cruise, and a Rain Forest project. In the evening, the Prime Minister will participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations, which will feature the Ekta Parade by security forces. Chirag Bhoraniya, Akashvani News, Ahmedabad.“

 

Prime Minister Modi began his two day Gujarat visit from Banaskantha this morning. He launched development projects worth more than 14 thousand crore rupees including state-of-the-art Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Center and Banas Bio CNG plants in Radhanpur and Tharad. Upon reaching Banaskantha this morning the Prime Minister held a roadshow and was accorded a grand welcome.

 

The Prime Minister also released the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to nearly 19 thousand crore rupees. Addressing the gathering Mr Modi said, farmers are one of the most important pillars of Viksit Bharat.

 

 

Speaking about the global economic uncertainty, Mr Modi said India’s rapid growth brings new hope for the world. He said, the tensions in the Gulf are ongoing, but the government did not pass on the burden of increased fertilizer prices to the farmers. The Prime Minister also called upon people especially the youth, to take part in the Run for Unity to be organised across the nation tomorrow.

 

 

<><><> 

Extreme poverty in the country has declined from 27.1 per cent in 2011 to 2.6 per cent in 2023. The World Bank’s Poverty and Equity report this month has highlighted country’s progress as one of the fastest poverty declines in the world. In a social media post, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that over 49 crore people have moved above the lower-middle-income poverty line during the same period. She mentioned that employment in India also increased by 13.4 crore people between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the increase in the working-age population. She said that rural women accounted for much of the employment gain, and both rural and urban households experienced substantial welfare gains.

The Finance Minister said, access to electricity reached 99 percent of the population. Ms Sitharaman said the government’s sustained policy efforts are yielding tangible results, strengthening the foundations for inclusive growth and greater economic opportunity.

 

<><><> 

 

Government today announced that population census will be conducted across the country, except in snow-bound and poll-bound states, from 25th of January to 28th of February next year. Home Ministry issued a notification declaring the census of population in all states and Union Territories except Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir. A revisional round will be held from 1st to 5th March, 2027. There shall be an option for self-enumeration from 10th of January to 24th of January for the conduct of the census.

 

<><><> 

 

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released draft ‘Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services’ for stakeholders’ comments. The draft has been placed on TRAI’s website.

The Ministry said, the government had released the ‘India AI Governance Guidelines’ in February this year to harness the benefits of Artificial Intelligence for inclusive development and global competitiveness, while addressing risks it may pose to individuals and society.

 

<><><> 

 

Home Minister Amit Shah today said the BJP would implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in Uttar Pradesh, expressing confidence that the party would return to power in the state after assembly elections next year. Addressing the BJP State Working Committee meeting in Lucknow today, he urged the party workers to work with full commitment to secure another victory with a clear majority. He credited party workers for the BJP’s victories in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections.

 

 

<><><> 

 

A helicopter travelling from Badrinath Dham to the Sahastradhara helipad in Dehradun crashed in the Hathi Parvat hills above Chai village in the Joshimath area of Chamoli district this afternoon. All six people on board, including the pilot, died in the accident.

According to Secretary of Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, information about the crash was received at around 2 PM. All the passengers on board were from Karnataka.

 

Governor Dr. Dhal Singh Bisen and Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed deep grief over the loss of lives and conveyed their condolences to the bereaved families. Chief Minister Dhami has also directed a detailed investigation into the causes of the accident.

<><><> 

 

In West Bengal, around 7 thousand people living along the Sankosh River in Alipurduar district have been shifted to safer locations following a rise in the river’s water level caused by a glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan. The Sankosh River has risen by nearly two feet since morning. The river flows along the inter-state boundary between West Bengal and Assam. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The precautionary evacuation was carried out on Thursday night following reports of a glacial lake breach in Bhutan, which raised fears of possible flooding in areas along the Sankosh River. More than seven thousand people were evacuated and accommodated in eighteen relief camps. Several residents from neighbouring Assam also took shelter in relief camps in Kumargram, near the Assam border in Alipurduar district. Although the river’s water level rose slightly on Friday afternoon, officials said it was still below the danger mark and had not reached an alarming level. The administration continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure the safety of people living in vulnerable areas. SandIpon Dasgupta RNU Kolkata.“

 

<><><> 

 

The aftermath of Cyclone Arnab has left devastation trail in large parts of southern Odisha. Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal are among the worst-affected districts. Although floodwaters are receding several villages remain marooned, and the suffering of affected people continues to mount. Landslides, damaged roads and disrupted rail services have compounded the crisis, even as rescue and relief operations are being intensified. More from our Correspondent –

 

 

 

“Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has conducted an aerial survey of the flood-hit districts and directed officials to expedite relief operations. President Droupadi Murmu today spoke to Chief Minister Mr. Majhi and was apprised of the flood situation in Odisha. Meanwhile, thirty additional officers have been deployed in Ganjam. The Coast Guard, NDRF and ODRAF are engaged in rescuing stranded people, with helicopter support. Train services have also been severely disrupted, with several cancellations. In Kandhamal, three members of a family, including a nine-month-old infant, were killed when a landslide buried their house under mud and debris in Dangesi village. Landslides have also damaged roads and paralysed normal life. Meanwhile, the rising Jalaka river has triggered fresh flood concerns in low-lying areas of northern Odisha. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

<><><> 

 

A low pressure area, remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over north Chhattisgarh and adjoining East Madhya Pradesh persisted over the region today. Meanwhile, another low pressure area over South Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman Nicobar Island persisted over the region.

<><><> 

 

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) will launch the NVS-03 navigation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota tonight. GSLV-F18 rocket in its milestone 20th flight will carry the satellite at 11.51 pm. It aims to boost India’s independent NavIC system by deploying an advanced satellite equipped with an indigenous atomic clock.

<><><> 

Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush with extensive crowd management preparations underway at at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Udhna railway station in Gujarat is an important example of a station having the modern passenger holding area is especially beneficial for migrant passengers travelling to their hometowns across different parts of the country during the festive season. The facility has been equipped with 10 ticket counters, 120 seats, 55 CCTV cameras, six electronic train display boards, a public announcement system and Wi-Fi connectivity. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

<><><> 

 

Manisha Bhanwala scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the Wrestling World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. She also became only the second Indian wrestler to claim a world championship title, after Sushil Kumar, who won the men’s 66-kilogram gold in 2010. Manisha clinched the women’s 59-kilogram gold with a remarkable 8-6 comeback victory over American wrestler Abigail Nette in the final.

 

<><><> 

 

In Men’s cricket, hosts New Zealand defeated India by 87 runs in the fourth T20 International at Eden Park in Auckland. Chasing a massive target of 260 runs, India managed to score 172 for nine in their allotted 20 overs. For the visitors, Tilak Varma top-scored with 35 runs, while Naman Dhir contributed 28.

Earlier, put into bat first, New Zealand posted a massive 259 for seven, powered by a spectacular century by Glenn Phillips scoring 107 runs off 49 balls.

 

<><><> 

 

Prasar Bharati has brought laurels to India, with Nongmaithem Nandakumar Singh winning the prestigious ABU Broadcast Engineering Excellence Award 2026 for his outstanding contribution to broadcast technology and innovation.

 

<><><>

THE HEADLINES:

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi to launch development projects worth over 14,000 crore rupees from Banaskantha in Gujarat tomorrow; To also release 24th instalment of PM-KISAN scheme, amounting to 19,000 crore rupees.
  2. Union Minister Piyush Goyal says, proposed India-US trade deal will protect farmers’ interests and give country a competitive advantage.
  3. Finance Ministry projects country’s GDP Growth at 7.35 per cent in second quarter of current fiscal.
  4. Supreme Court says, banks must compensate digital fraud victims in case of negligence.
  5. IMD issues red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.
  6. And Indian wrestler Manisha advances to women’s 59 kg final at World Championships in Kazakhstan.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Gujarat, beginning tomorrow. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 14 thousand crore rupees in Banaskantha tomorrow. The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension). He will also release the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to 19 thousand crore rupees. He will also visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre cattle farm in Banaskantha. The Centre will strengthen bovine breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technologies, accelerating breed improvement by 10 to 20 times. Thereafter, the Prime Minister will travel to Ekta Nagar, Kevadia and inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026.

 

 

 

On Saturday, Prime Minister Modi will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over four hundred crore rupees in Ekta Nagar.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that India’s proposed trade deal with the United States will protect farmers’ interests and give the country a competitive advantage. He assured that the agreement would not compromise the sensitive interests of farmers or any other stakeholders. Mr. Goyal was addressing the three-day National Conference on India’s Industrial Transformation in New Delhi today.

 

 

 

The Minister also said India has signed nine trade agreements covering 38 developed nations, with a combined GDP of 60 trillion dollars.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

India’s economic momentum remains strong, with the economy projected to grow by 7.35 per cent in the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27. According to the Finance Ministry’s monthly economic review for October, released today, growth is supported by stronger industrial output, higher energy consumption, increased port traffic, robust GST collections and rising automobile sales. Here is a Report:

 

 

 

“The report highlighted that country’s external sector continued to demonstrate resilience last month amid heightened global uncertainty with total exports of merchandise and services growing by 11 per cent Year on Year. Merchandise exports, which grew by over 23 per cent Year on Year, were the principal driver of this growth, led by electronics and engineering goods. Supported by a steady services surplus, the overall trade deficit narrowed during the period. The report noted that robust domestic demand, sustained investment activity, a resilient financial sector and proactive supply-side management have underpinned India’s growth resilience so far. It said, amidst elevated crude oil prices, higher food inflation and uncertain outlook for the Kharif crop, sustaining economic activity while safeguarding price stability will be the focus of policymakers in the second half of the financial year. Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Supreme Court has said banks and other financial institutions must be held accountable for losses suffered by victims of digital fraud. The court observed that victims of offences such as digital arrest scams should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if the fraud is found to have resulted from a financial institution’s failure to exercise due diligence. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said, it will examine the Reserve Bank of India’s proposed Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026. The directions are expected to be notified by 30th of November and made operational by 31st of December.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Super Specialty (NEET-SS) 2026 will be conducted on December 11 and 12 this year. In a notice issued today, the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) said the examination would be held in computer-based mode at various examination centres across the country. The last date for submitting the application form is November 18th of this year.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda has said that India has made significant progress in healthcare and digital service delivery over the past ten years. Addressing a function in New Delhi today, Mr Nadda said, the number of AIIMS has increased from one institute to 23, and the number of medical colleges has risen from 387 to 863. He said, through the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, the health records, vaccination, and screening of crores of people are being digitized, so that health services can become more accessible, effective, and transparent. Mr Nadda highlighted that 98 crore ABHA cards have been generated so far.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana completed two years today. Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the scheme in October 2024 to extend the benefits of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) to all citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status.

 

 

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said, the scheme aims to provide dignified, cashless healthcare coverage to around six crore eligible senior citizens.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

World Stroke Day is being observed today to raise awareness about stroke and the importance of recognising its warning signs. This year’s campaign message, ‘Every Minute Counts – Know the Signs of Stroke’, reminds everyone that timely action can save lives.

 

 

On the occasion, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda said, sudden facial drooping, weakness in an arm, or difficulty speaking should never be ignored.

 

 

Talking to Akashvani News, Chief of the Neurosciences Centre at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, Dr Shailesh B Gaikwad said that the symptoms of the stroke include sudden loss or blurring of vision, double vision, loss of balance, and difficulty in walking. Dr Gaikwad emphasized if such symptoms are visible then the patients should immediately transfer to stroke ready hospital for treatment.

 

 

{<><><>}

 

 

The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards. It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight. Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.

 

 

 

In Odisha, torrential rain following Cyclone Arnab has triggered severe flooding and landslides in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts, leaving dozens of villages marooned. More from our Correspondent:

 

 

 

“Incessant rainfall following Cyclone Arnab has affected nearly three hundred villages in Ganjam district, with around 70 reported marooned. More than 2000 people have been stranded, particularly in Sanakhemundi, Aska, Dharakote, Sorada and Patrapur blocks. The Rushikulya river at Purushottampur has risen to 19 metres, above its danger level of 16.8 metres. The Bahuda and Bansadhara rivers are also in spate. Berhampur has witnessed severe waterlogging, while a stretch of National Highway 326 in Gajapati has been washed away, cutting road connectivity. The Indian Coast Guard has begun helicopter evacuations, while rescue teams are assisting affected people. The East Coast Railway has cancelled 20 trains and many other trains have been diverted. The IMD has warned of further rain in Odisha. A new low-pressure area over the South Andaman Sea is likely to intensify into a depression around this Saturday. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

 

Heavy rain continued across Chhattisgarh today under the influence of Cyclone Arnab. As a precautionary measure, schools in several districts of the state have been closed till tomorrow. A report:

 

 

“Cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ has weakened into a low-pressure area. It is expected to move towards northern Chhattisgarh over the next twelve hours. As a result, rain is occurring today in several districts across central and northern Chhattisgarh. The Meteorological Department has issued an ‘Orange Alert’ for certain districts within the Surguja, Bilaspur, and Raipur divisions, while a ‘Red Alert’ has been issued for Raigarh and its surrounding areas. In the Bastar division, districts including Sukma have been experiencing rainfall for the past two days. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke with Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai over the phone today to assess the current situation in the state in light of the cyclone. Rahul Sinha, All India Radio News, Raipur.”

 

 

 

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu today visited cyclone-affected areas in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district and assured affected families of all possible assistance. More from our correspondent:

 


“During his visit to Vetlapalem, the Chief Minister inspected submerged paddy fields and damaged coconut plantations and interacted with affected farmers. He announced compensation of one thousand five hundred rupees for each damaged coconut tree. He also assured twenty-five kilograms of rice and essential commodities to cyclone-affected families. At a rehabilitation camp in Gachakayalapora village, he directed officials to restore damaged houses and address fishermen’s boat registration issues. Mr. Naidu said a Central team would visit the state tomorrow to assess the damage. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has assured full support from the Centre. Ravala Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

 

 

An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Indian wrestler Manisha Bhanwala advanced to the women’s 59 kg final at the World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan today. Manisha defeated home favourite Altyn Shagayeva by a dominant 10-nil by fall to book her spot in the gold medal bout. She will face Abigail Nette of the United States in the final tomorrow.

 

 

Meanwhile, Tanu Sharma won the bronze medal in the women’s 72 kg category after defeating Precious Bell of the United States, 9-5.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

In Hockey, India continued their winning streak at Men’s Asian Champions Trophy by defeating China 5-2 in their second league match at Jalandhar in Punjab this evening.

 

 

<><><>

THE HEADLINES:-

  1. Government approves schemes to make country a global manufacturing hub of containers and sports goods; Also gives nod to Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana to strengthen grassroot governance.

  2. BJP-NDA sweeps Karnataka Legislative Council elections; Counting continues for MLC polls in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra.

  3. Heavy rain batters northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha as Cyclone Arnab weakens after landfall, leaving trail of destruction.

  4. Ministry of External Affairs says, 22 Indian nationals, including 14 seafarers killed in West Asia conflict so far; Reiterates India’s firm stand against terror financing and cross-border terrorism amid ongoing FATF meeting in Paris.

  5. Two high-speed trains collide in Toledo province of Spain, killing 68 people.

  6. And, Indian Women shine in Sports; Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Dhochak win silver medals at World Wrestling Championships; Cricket Team clean sweep three-match ODI series against Zimbabwe.

<><><>

         

The government today approved several key initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing and promoting rural governance. The decisions were taken at a Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Briefing the media in New Delhi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the details.
         

Mr Vaishnaw said, the Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme with a total outlay of ten thousand crore rupees over 13 years, up to the financial year 2039-40. The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India.

           

The Cabinet has also given nod to the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods.

 

         

The Cabinet has also cleared Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, with a total financial outlay of seven thousand 395 crore rupees. The scheme will be implemented over five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31 to empower Gram Panchayats and strengthen grassroots governance.

           

         

Meanwhile, the Cabinet has also approved a three per cent increase in Dearness Allowance for Central Government employees and Dearness Relief for pensioners, with effect from the first of July, this year.

<><><> 

         

Counting for votes is underway Legislative Council elections in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, while results for all four seats in Karnataka have been declared. Elections were held for a total of 28 seats across the four states.
         

In Karnataka, the BJP-led NDA has dominated the Legislative Council elections, with the BJP winning three seats and its ally Janata Dal (Secular) securing one seat.
         

In Uttar Pradesh, results have been declared for eight out of 11 Legislative Council seats, with the BJP winning five seats and the Samajwadi Party securing three.   In Bihar, results for six of the eight seats have been declared, with the BJP winning two seats, while the JD(U), RJD, Jan Suraaj and an Independent candidate have secured one seat each.
         

In Maharashtra, out of a total of five seats, the BJP and Shiv Sena have so far secured a seat each in the Legislative Council elections.
         

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today took a dig at the Congress party over the MLC elections held using ballot papers.  In a social media post, Mr Modi questioned the Congress party’s performance, asking how many seats it has won in these elections.

<><><> 

         

Cyclone Arnab has weakened into a deep depression after making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast leaving a trail of destruction. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm crossed the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Narsapur and southwest of Yanam, early this morning. The system is continuing to weaken as it drifts slowly north-northwestward towards Chhattisgarh and Telangana.

         

The weather system is triggering heavy rainfall across northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. Relief and rescue operations continue in the worst-affected regions of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha following the landfall of the cyclone. Over one lakh 80 thousand people have been evacuated to safer zones and relief shelters across the two states.         
         

Andhra Pradesh government has announced financial assistance for families and businesses affected by the cyclone. More from our correspondent.
                    

         

“Amaravati Meteorological Centre has forecast heavy rainfall over the next three hours in several districts of Andhra Pradesh, including Srikakulam, Eluru, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, NTR and Guntur. Strong winds reaching speeds of 50 to 60 kilometres per hour are also likely. In the past 12 hours, Visakhapatnam recorded 21 centimetres of rainfall, while Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts received 14 centimetres each. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to provide essential commodities to people whose houses have been inundated by the cyclone. The Chief Minister also stated that assistance of 10,000 rupees would be provided for partially damaged houses and 25,000 rupees for shops affected by the cyclone. Satyanarayana, Akashvani News, Visakhapatnam.”

  <><><>

         

In Odisha, the IMD has issued a red warning for six districts: Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Nabarangpur, Malkangiri and Rayagada. Flooding, damage to houses and disruptions to road and rail services remain major concerns. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has reviewed the situation, while authorities remain on high alert. We have a report:


         

“Cyclone Arnab continues to affect southern Odisha, with heavy rainfall and strong winds disrupting normal life in several areas. Several houses have reportedly been damaged in Jeypore and Pottangi. Four gates of Harbhangi Dam have been opened, and residents of low-lying areas have been alerted. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed the situation this evening at the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Rail services have been cancelled or regulated on several routes, while bus connectivity to southern Odisha has faced precautionary restrictions. Meanwhile, the IMD has said that another weather system is developing over the South Andaman Sea. An upper-air cyclonic circulation over the region is likely to trigger the formation of a low-pressure area within the next 24 hours. Prakash Dash, Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.” 

         

The cyclone has caused widespread damage in the Yanam region of Puducherry. Standing paddy crops have been inundated, while fishermen have suffered losses as large stocks of dried fish stored on coastal fish-drying platforms were damaged. Government has assured people of all necessary assistance.

         

The IMD has issued an orange colour warning for very heavy rainfall for Bihar, Chhattisgarh, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha tomorrow.

<><><> 

         

The External Affairs Ministry has said, twenty-two Indians, including 14 seafarers, have been killed so far in the ongoing West Asia conflict. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal expressed deep concern over the ongoing conflict.
           

         

Speaking about ongoing Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting in Paris, the spokesperson reiterated India’s firm stand against terror financing and cross-border terrorism.                         

 

 

<><><>

         

External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar today held talks with his Austrian counterpart, Beate Meinl-Reisinger, in New Delhi to strengthen bilateral cooperation and discuss key global issues. In a social media post, Dr. Jaishankar said they explored new avenues of cooperation in start-ups, space, skill development and mobility.
         

Earlier in the day, in his opening remarks, Dr. Jaishankar said India’s ties with the European Union had intensified and that New Delhi looked forward to the Free Trade Agreement coming into force in the coming months.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met his Japanese counterpart Koizumi Shinjiro, on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM)-Plus in Philippines. BRICS Member Nations have expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation. In the Joint Declaration which was unanimously adopted today at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum held in New Delhi, the member countries urged to ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. “BRICS nations have stressed on the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law. Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Puducherry, Telangana and Chhattisgarh have stepped up preparations as Cyclone Arnab has advanced towards the eastern coast. Cyclone Arnab will hit Bapatla and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm tomorrow forenoon. Talking exclusively to Akashvani, Director General of India Meteorological Department (IMD) Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said that during landfall the cyclone will have maximum sustained wind speed upto 125 to 150 kilometres per hour. Dr. Mohapatra has cautioned people of destructive winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding.

 

Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh tomorrow.

 

The Ministry of Home Affairs has directed State Governments to keep a close watch, monitor the situation in their areas regularly and take appropriate precautionary measures in view of Cyclone Arnab. In an advisory, the Ministry has suggested for evacuating the people living in coastal areas to safer places and complete suspension of fishing operations.

 

In Andhra Pradesh, state authorities have stepped up preparedness as heavy to extremely heavy rainfall and coastal inundation are expected in several areas.

 

“The cyclone was centred 170 kilometres south-southeast of Visakhapatnam this evening. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is occurring in several districts, including Konaseema, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli, with isolated places likely to receive 21 centimetres or more of rainfall. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, while district administrations have established control rooms and intensified preparedness and relief measures. The State Disaster Management Authority has warned of seawater surges in vulnerable coastal areas and urged fishermen and residents of low-lying areas to remain alert. Meanwhile, more than 53 trains have been cancelled today and tomorrow as a precautionary measure. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

In Odisha, the state government has mobilised disaster-response teams and placed vulnerable districts on high alert. Rail services face widespread disruption, fishing operations have been suspended, and educational institutions in several districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after tomorrow.

 

“Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab’s pre-landfall process has started with rains in south and coastal Odisha, as the powerful weather system moves closer to the eastern coastline. According to the latest available India Meteorological Department bulletin, Arnab is about 380 kilometres south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha. Even as Odisha is on high alert, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has deployed eight ministers to oversee preparedness in vulnerable districts likely to be badly affected, while rescue teams, evacuation arrangements and relief shelters have been readied. Red warnings cover vulnerable southern districts, with heavy to extremely heavy rainfall threatening low-lying areas, roads, power lines and standing crops; more than 60 train services have been cancelled across the affected network and other services modified. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. The administration is racing against time to minimise damage and ensure public safety. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast very heavy rainfall in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh from Tuesday to Thursday in view of the approaching weather system.

Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have stepped up their preparedness measures to deal with the potential impact of the developing cyclone.

The Odisha government has mobilised disaster response teams and stepped up precautionary measures. Our correspondent has the details:

 

“The system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the Wednesday forenoon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour and gusts reaching 140 kilometres per hour. Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri are among the districts facing heightened risks, with a red warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on Wednesday. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has directed the administration to ensure preparedness and minimise casualties. Around 60 ODRAF teams and 17 NDRF teams have been deployed, while 225 Fire Services teams remain on high alert. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five southern districts will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while authorities are preparing for evacuations and possible disruption to transport, power supply and agricultural activities. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

 

Andhra Pradesh is also on high alert as a very severe cyclonic storm is forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. More from our correspondent:

 

“Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has reviewed the state’s preparedness and directed officials to remain alert. Ten NDRF and eleven SDRF teams are ready for rescue operations. Officials are preparing evacuation plans, relief camps, and arrangements for food, drinking water and medical services. Control rooms have been set up in all coastal districts, with helpline numbers made available to the public. The government has directed officials to remove dangerous hoardings. The Electricity Department has kept 25-thousand poles ready for emergency repairs. Hospitals have been directed to provide round-the-clock services. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.“

The auspicious festival of Sharad Purnima, also known as Lakshmi Puja, is being celebrated across the country with religious fervour and traditional enthusiasm. Devotees are offering special prayers to Goddess Lakshmi, seeking peace, prosperity and well-being for their families. A key ritual of the festival involves preparing kheer, a sweet rice pudding, and placing it in the open sky under the full moon overnight. According to traditional beliefs, the full moon on Sharad Purnima showers nectar-like rays, which are believed to impart special qualities to the offering. By the next morning, the dessert is offered as prasad and shared with family members. For generations, this ritual has has been part of  the festival.

In West Bengal, the festival is being celebrated with devotion across the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions. Among the local Nepali Gorkha community, the occasion is observed as Kojagrat Purnima, with devotees traditionally keeping vigil through the night and offering prayers to Goddess Lakshmi.
